advances: An exact prescribed-centroid obstruction in one integer and one continuous dimension. The distinct scalar benchmark is strictly satisfied in this family.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $l=r-w$. The second differences of $r,l$ are $(-3/4,-15/4,-3/4)$ and $(1/4,5/4,9/4)$, respectively. Thus the interpolated upper roof is concave and the lower roof convex. All widths are positive, including between sampled bases by interpolation. The body has exactly the given intervals on the integer bases. The sums are $\sum_iw_i=107$, $\sum_i iw_i=0$, and $\sum_i w_i r_i=\tfrac12\sum_i w_i^2=4657/4$. The continuous first moment is $\tfrac12\sum_i(r_i^2-l_i^2)=0$. In particular the centroid is interior to its fiber.

For the two orientations let $v_i^+=r_i$, $v_i^-=w_i-r_i$ and set $[b]_0^w=\min(w,\max(0,b))$. The raw mass is $F_\pm(a)=\sum_i[v_i^\pm+ai]_0^{w_i}$. By the finite slope rule in dcb05945476b6c35, the knots occur at $-v_i^\pm/i,(w_i-v_i^\pm)/i$ for $i\ne0$, with affine interpolation of masses between them and constant tails. Substitution gives the complete tables, with $A=8560a$ and $V=4280F$.

| $A_+$ | $V_+$ | $A_-$ | $V_-$ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| -74534 | 230723 | -123202 | 225525 |
| -71414 | 232283 | -119474 | 227389 |
| -19015 | 232283 | -62243 | 227389 |
| -14797 | 228065 | -59737 | 229895 |
| 59737 | 228065 | 14797 | 229895 |
| 62243 | 230571 | 19015 | 225677 |
| 119474 | 230571 | 71414 | 225677 |
| 123202 | 232435 | 74534 | 227237 |

The positive and negative minima are $45613/856$ and $45105/856$. The latter occurs exactly on the left constant tail, including its endpoint. The pure-base closed cuts through the centroid have masses $659/10$ and $663/10$, including the entire central boundary fiber. Any containing halfspace can be moved inward to the centroid. Moving an oblique through-centroid halfspace strictly outward adds positive length in the central fiber, so there are no additional oblique minimizers off the centroid.

For either orientation the bound $v_i^\pm+ai\le W$ is satisfied at $i=0$, and the other four inequalities give the interval with endpoints $\max_{i<0}(W-v_i^\pm)/i$ and $\min_{i>0}(W-v_i^\pm)/i$. Multiplying by $8560$ gives $[-48119,93059]$ and $[-88841,45613]$. Each restricted interval contains a minimizing knot or plateau for its restriction, as read from the table. The restricted minima are $45613/856$ and $225677/4280$, respectively. Moving a containing boundary inward only reduces all margin upper endpoints, so allowing the boundary off the centroid does not improve the restricted minimum. Finally $225677/4280-45105/856=19/535$ and $\sum_iw_i^2/(2W)=23285/504$, giving the stated gap to that separate scalar benchmark.

statement:
At the integer bases $i=-2,-1,0,1,2$, in that order, take the intervals $[r_i-w_i,r_i]$ with
$$
w=(92/5,223/10,126/5,231/10,18),\qquad
r=59737/4280+(0,0,-3/4,-21/4,-21/2).
$$
They are the exact sampled fibers of the convex body with adjacent affine interpolation of their endpoints. Their mixed length is $107$, their true mixed centroid is $(0,0)$, and $W=\max_i w_i=126/5$. The raw closed-halfspace depth at that centroid is $45105/856$, with normalized depth $45105/91592$. All minimizing caps are $-x+az\ge0$ with $a\le-61601/4280$. If both orientations $\sigma x+az\ge0$, $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, are allowed but every upper endpoint in the margin coordinate $\sigma x+az$ must be at most $W$, the minimum increases to $225677/4280$, an excess of $19/535$. The unrestricted depth exceeds $\sum_iw_i^2/(2W)$ by $43765/6741$.
title: Five actual intervals obstruct a bounded-upper minimizing centroid cap
